en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on the Tamāla Flower (Tamālapupphiyavagga), Number Eight:
The Apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipūjaka.
“The Blessed One named Sumedha,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
out of compassion for the future, [taught].”
The Conqueror exerted himself in striving.
As he walked back and forth, that Lord of bipeds, the Tathāgata, [attained enlightenment].
I offered a handful of girinelā flowers to the Buddha;
by that clarity of mind,
Urged on by the root of that white virtue,
for thirty thousand eons I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
In the twenty-three hundredth aeon,
there was a kṣatriya named Sunela,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
I was alone and possessed of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Muṭṭhipūjaka speak these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Muṭṭhipūjaka.
